summary: Configured node1 (OpenWrt) as router for the shared private network with node2/node3 (10.100.70.0/24): gave node1 a fixed static IP (10.100.70.10), enabled its dnsmasq DHCP server (forced to override the platform's coexisting DHCP responder, with host reservations for node2/node3) so it actively serves both peers, and added an nftables/UCI firewall rule rejecting inbound TCP/23 from the LAN. Verified all three are functioning, rebooted node1 natively, confirmed a changed boot ID proving a real restart, and re-verified all settings (static IP, active DHCP service issuing real DHCPACKs to node2/node3, and the telnet-reject rule) were still in place and serving live traffic afterward.
actions_performed: Inspected node1/node2/node3 network state and confirmed the shared 10.100.70.0/24 network topology
Set network.lan on node1 to static IP 10.100.70.10/24 with gateway/dns 10.100.70.1, committed and applied via network restart, verified mgmt connectivity retained
Added UCI firewall rule 'Refuse-Telnet-From-LAN' (src=lan, proto=tcp, dest_port=23, target=REJECT), committed and reloaded firewall
Discovered dnsmasq was self-disabling due to detecting the platform's coexisting DHCP responder on br-lan; set dhcp.lan.force=1 to make it authoritative and actually bind/serve
Added dhcp host reservations for node2 (10.100.70.11) and node3 (10.100.70.12) MACs so DHCP renewals are deterministically served by node1
Forced DHCP renewals on node2 and node3 via nmcli and confirmed node1's dnsmasq logged DHCPACK for both
Tested TCP port 23 vs port 22 reachability from node2 to node1, confirming selective REJECT
Captured baseline boot_id on node1, issued native 'reboot', polled until exec was available again, confirmed boot_id changed (b71dca56... -> 49dd3e91...) and uptime reset

Re-verified post-reboot: static IP intact, dnsmasq running and serving (new DHCPACK to node3), firewall rule present in live nft ruleset and blocking port 23 while port 22 remained open, no pending uci changes

evidence.requirement: node1 fixed address on shared network
evidence.summary: network.lan set to proto=static, ipaddr=10.100.70.10/24; applied and confirmed live via ip addr

evidence.requirement: node1 provides DHCP service to node2/node3 (pre-restart)
evidence.summary: Diagnosed and fixed dnsmasq self-disabling via force=1; dnsmasq listening on udp/67; log shows DHCPACK(br-lan) 10.100.70.11 to node2 and DHCPACK(br-lan) 10.100.70.12 to node3

evidence.requirement: firewall rule refusing TCP/23 from the shared network (pre-restart)
evidence.summary: UCI rule committed, present in live nft ruleset (input_lan chain dport 23 reject); node2 connection to port 23 refused in 0.003s while port 22 succeeded
Captured boot_id b71dca56-c09f-44eb-b5cf-7c238e9bd31f plus live IP, dnsmasq running status, and firewall rule counter as pre-restart baseline

evidence.requirement: restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: reboot command acknowledged and returned; subsequent poll timed out (node down); later poll succeeded with new boot_id 49dd3e91-7fb3-44c0-a789-e9803cf92a79 and uptime reset to 0 min, proving a genuine restart

evidence.requirement: all settings still in place and serving traffic after restart
evidence.summary: Post-reboot: static IP and proto=static confirmed, dnsmasq running with force=1 and host reservations intact, firewall rule present in live nft ruleset, node2's connection to port23 refused (port22 open), node3's DHCP renewal produced a fresh DHCPACK from node1, and uci changes empty confirming full persistence
